Reunification
The need for reunification could come from two separate, but related, types of events:
Events where those separated are all impacted by a disaster and end up in different locations due to evacuations or routes being impacted for a variety of reasons.
Events where individuals or family members not impacted by a disaster are looking for family members whose whereabouts are unknown due to an ongoing incident.
In both instances, it is important for organizations/jurisdictions to think through how they would handle the need to reunify families.
FEMA has developed this Exercise Starter Kit (ESK) with sample documents for your organization/jurisdiction to use to conduct your own exercise on essential aspects of reunification. These materials provide planning considerations and discussion questions for internal conversations and decisions around two core capabilities within the
Recovery
mission area:
Operational coordination
Public information and warning
The ESK consists of two modules based around the following scenarios:
Module 1:
Incident Occurs
Module 2:
Reunification
